# Introduction to R {#sec-intro2R}

Throughout this script we use the free software R for data analysis, simulation and plotting. The introduction to R is now a separate online book, which I also use in other courses:

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## 💻 Coding Intro

[**www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/**](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/)

For this course, you only need the part **Introduction to R**. The part on Python is optional.
:::

## What You Need for This Course

Please work through the following chapters of the [Coding Intro](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/) before (or while) working on the next chapters of this script:

1. [The first steps in R](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-01-Getting-Started.html)
2. [Create and load data sets](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-02-Datasets.html)
3. [Simple programming](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-03-Programming.html)
4. [Functions](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-04-Functions.html)
5. [Plotting in R](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-05-Plotting.html) (Not relevant for the exam, but important for writing your thesis.)
6. [Monte Carlo simulations](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-06-Monte-Carlo-Simulations.html)
7. [Regression analysis](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-07-Regression.html)

The chapter [Some notes on useful packages](https://www.dliebl.com/Script-Coding-Intros/R-08-Notes-on-useful-packages.html) is only  optional. In this script, we use base R for computations and plots.

## Self-Check

You are well prepared for the following chapters if you can do the following in R:

* create vectors and data frames, and select elements, e.g., `x[2]`, `x[x > 0]`, `data$column`,
* read a data set from a `.csv` file with `read.csv()`,
* compute simple summaries with `mean()`, `var()`, `sd()`, `sum()`, `table()`,
* write a simple function and a `for` loop,
* draw random numbers with `sample()` and `rnorm()`, and make them reproducible with `set.seed()`,
* plot data with `plot()`, `hist()`, `lines()`, `abline()`, `curve()` and `legend()`.
